written.myAnswer: Lower molecular mass covalent compounds have weak intermolecular forces, so little energy is needed to separate their molecules. They therefore exist as gases or low-boiling liquids.

HF molecules form strong hydrogen bonds because hydrogen is bonded to highly electronegative fluorine. HCl molecules have weaker dipole–dipole attractions, so HF has a higher boiling point and is a liquid while HCl is a gas.

I₂ molecules are larger and have more electrons than Cl₂ molecules, giving them stronger intermolecular forces. More energy is needed to separate I₂ molecules, so iodine is solid while chlorine is a gas.
